description: Cross-binding conformance for the SCALAR half of esm-spec §6.3 'Inline array data' and §6.6.2 'Shaped values': a scalar on a SHAPED variable keeps its broadcast meaning -- the one value applies to every element -- and the same union applies to a shaped variable's declared `default`. The shaped UNKNOWN side of that rule was already pinned (a state's scalar `default` seeds every cell of the state vector); the shaped PARAMETER side was not, and all three executing bindings got it wrong in their own vocabulary (EarthSciML/EarthSciAST#219). Rust left the parameter in its positional scalar `params` vector, so every per-cell read -- the `index(p, k)` a document writes AND the gather `index_array_leaves_by_loops` inserts for a bare whole-array right-hand side -- indexed a scalar and resolved to NaN; the solve then died at t = 0 with `Exceeded maximum number of nonlinear solver failures` naming no parameter at all. Python bound it in the scalar `param_values` map, where a bare read broadcast correctly but `index(p, k)` raised 'index applied to scalar value'. Julia REFUSED the document outright with `E_TREEWALK_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE`, because `_partition_variables` requires an array-shaped parameter to be backed by `const_arrays` or `param_arrays` and a scalar default reached neither. The fix is the same shape in all three: the value is BROADCAST onto the declared grid and bound on the array channel each binding already uses for a shaped parameter's inline column, so the scalar and array spellings of §6.3 differ only in what they say, never in what the runtime does. Non-vacuity is structural: `phi` integrates the broadcast parameter DIRECTLY and asserts min == max over four cells (the sharpest statement of 'every element'), while `theta` gathers it at the same cell as a SECOND shaped parameter whose array-valued `default` has pairwise-distinct cells -- so a binding that broadcast the wrong operand, or filled only one cell, disagrees somewhere rather than passing on a coincidence. The four tests hold the #219 bisection axis inside ONE document, plus the §6.6.2 precedence arm: the declared scalar, a SCALAR `parameter_overrides` value, the ARRAY `parameter_overrides` spelling of the SAME parameter, and a SCALAR override of the OTHER shaped parameter -- the one whose declared `default` is an array, which the override must replace rather than lose to. The array arm passed before the fix and still passes, so a regression on either spelling is caught separately. Julia is the reference binding; its `run_pde_tests` minted the golden.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator / inline test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; the in-process runner is a scalar expression evaluator with no state vector or array channel

fixtures.note: `ramp` is the shaped parameter under test (scalar `default` 0.5); `scale` is the array-valued control ([1,2,3,4]) that keeps every theta cell distinct. `phi` integrates ramp[k] alone, `theta` integrates ramp[k]*scale[k].

assertions.note: 0.5 broadcast into cell 1 and integrated for one unit of time
and into cell 4: the far end of the grid, not just the first cell
min == max over four cells: 'the one value applies to every element'
the shaped UNKNOWN's own scalar default -- the half of §6.3 that already worked
1 + 0.5*scale[4]: distinct from cell 1, so the array control is live
§6.6.2: a SCALAR parameter_overrides value on a shaped parameter broadcasts too
the ARRAY spelling of the same union on the same parameter -- the arm that passed before the fix
§6.6.2 precedence: a SCALAR override of `scale` REPLACES its declared array default -- 1 + 0.5*3, not 1 + 0.5*scale[1]
the same at cell 4, where the dropped-override reading would give 3.0
min == max: the override broadcast over the WHOLE grid, flattening the array default's profile
`ramp` is untouched by the override, so a leak into the other shaped parameter fails here
